evidence.finding: Deterministic recalculation found an exact -26.0-point discrepancy in all 11 intervals from 09:15 through 11:45; all five earlier intervals matched the formula.
Post-incident queue service-level means remained 80.30%–92.11%, materially above center dashboard readings of 48.42%–69.24%.
Queue staffing was unchanged across the incident boundary: General Service 19, Billing 12, Account Support 11, and Escalations 7 agents.
Offered calls increased 28.10% in General Service and 23.85% in Account Support, creating localized pressure but not explaining the fixed reporting offset.

primary_root_cause_detail: A service-level reporting defect began exactly at 09:15. Every subsequent center interval was understated by exactly 26.0 percentage points relative to the defined count-based formula, while every pre-incident interval reconciled.
recommended_actions: Remove the erroneous 26-point adjustment from the dashboard calculation or transformation.
Recalculate and backfill center service level from 09:15 onward using the defined formula.
Add automated interval-level reconciliation between reported service level and component counts.
Separately monitor localized demand pressure in General Service and Account Support.

rejected_hypotheses.reason: Demand increased only in selected queues; Billing was flat and Escalations declined. Volume changes cannot explain an exact fixed 26-point metric discrepancy.
Staffed-agent counts were unchanged in every queue across the incident boundary.
AHT changes were small and mixed across queues, with no broad sustained increase.
Localized queue pressure existed, especially in Account Support, but queue performance remained substantially healthier than the center dashboard and cannot explain the arithmetic offset.
Queues continued processing calls with post-incident mean service levels of 80.30%–92.11%; the observed dashboard effect is fully explained by the reporting mismatch.

stakeholder_summary: The dashboard alert was caused primarily by a confirmed reporting defect, not a center-wide operational collapse. The defect began at the incident boundary and understated every subsequent interval by exactly 26 points. Some localized demand pressure occurred, but staffing remained stable and queue-level results were materially healthier than the reported center metric.
